mistake_content: Hardcoded wait using time.sleep - Use of time.sleep() instead of dynamic waits can lead to flaky and slow tests. Pattern: 'time.sleep('. Recommendation: Replace time.sleep() with WebDriverWait and expected_conditions.
solution: Replace time.sleep(5) with dynamic wait using self.driver.wait_for_object(). Before clicking the edit shortcut print toggle button, wait for the element to be ready using: self.driver.wait_for_object("edit_shortcut_print_toggle_locator", timeout=30, raise_e=False). This ensures the element is present and interactable before attempting the click action. Alternatively, if the previous action should complete before proceeding, add change_check parameter to verify the UI state transition.

mistake_content: The test class 'Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut' incorrectly inherits from 'unittest.TestCase' instead of 'object'. The current code shows: 'class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(unittest.TestCase):' but according to HPX automation framework standards, it should be 'class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(object):'. This violates the pytest-based architecture that the HPX framework is built upon.
solution: Change the class declaration from 'class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(unittest.TestCase):' to 'class Test_Suite_01_Add_Shortcut(object):'. The HPX automation framework uses pytest as its test framework, not unittest. Test classes must inherit from 'object' to properly integrate with pytest's test discovery, fixture management, and marker system. Mixing unittest.TestCase with pytest creates conflicts in test execution, fixture handling, and reporting. The standard pattern documented in Section 7 (TEST FILE ANATOMY & CONVENTIONS) explicitly shows: 'class Test_Suite_XX_<FeatureName>(object):'. This ensures compatibility with pytest decorators (@pytest.fixture, @pytest.mark), proper class-based setup patterns, and correct test execution flow.
